Note::any¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::any() const

Detect At Least One Passing Lane¶

any() reduces an entire Bool Note to one rank-zero Bool Note. It returns true as soon as one receiver lane is true; it returns false only when every lane is false or the receiver has no lanes.

There is no axis overload. A vector, matrix, or rank-three Note is treated as one Boolean population in row-major storage order. Shape affects which lanes belong to the receiver, but not the scalar shape of the result.

The operation is intentionally strict about dtype. It does not treat nonempty text as true, parse "true", or convert nonzero integers. Its input must be a defined Bool Note, normally produced by a predicate, comparison, Boolean composition, or pluss::note::make with Boolean values.

Reduction Contract¶

Receiver

Result

at least one lane is true

scalar Bool Note containing true

every lane is false

scalar Bool Note containing false

scalar Bool Note

the same truth value in a newly allocated scalar Note

empty Bool Note of any shape

scalar false

Text, Bytes, Int64, or Float64 Note

error

undefined Note

error

The empty result is false, the identity for disjunction. No candidate lane exists that could satisfy the condition.

any() scans contiguous one-byte Boolean storage and short-circuits at the first true lane. Its worst-case cost is O(numel()); a leading true lane makes the scan constant-time apart from creating the scalar result. It does not materialize a flattened Note or inspect text payloads.

Example 1: Find One Passing Lane¶

const auto checks = pluss::note::make({true, false, false});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(checks.any()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
true

Example 2: No Lane Passes¶

const auto checks = pluss::note::make({false, false});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(checks.any()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
false

Example 3: Reduce A Matrix Predicate¶

const auto cells = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"draft", "ready", "hold", "sent"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto ready = cells == "ready";

std::cout << pluss::note::print(ready) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(ready.any()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, dtype=Bool)
[
  [false, true], 
  [false, false]
]
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
true

All axes participate. The method answers whether the complete matrix contains a match, not which row contains one.

Example 4: Build A Compound Search¶

const auto names = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});
const auto selected = names.starts_with("A") | names.ends_with("s");

std::cout << pluss::note::print(selected) << '\n';
std::cout << "found=" << std::boolalpha << selected.any().bool_item() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, false, true]
found=true

Use the scalar Note result directly when the next operation accepts a Note. Call bool_item() only when native C++ control flow needs a bool.

Example 5: Scalar Input¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make(true).any()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
true

Example 6: Empty Disjunction¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<bool>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{0, 3});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(empty.any()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
false

If an empty domain should be an application error rather than a negative answer, check empty() before reducing.

Example 7: Invalid Receivers Reject¶

try { (void)pluss::note::make({"", "value"}).any(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "any Text: rejected\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::Note::undefined().any(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "any undefined: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

any Text: rejected
any undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • all: require every Boolean lane to pass.

  • operators: produce and combine shape-preserving Bool Notes.

  • empty: distinguish absence of lanes from an all-false population.
